sentences.text: ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE AKIL KURESHI)

The applicant, appellant has challenged the judgment and decree passed by the Civil Court dated 5.2.2014 under which the security deposit amount of Rs.15,50,000/- of the respondent, original plaintiff is ordered to be refunded.
According to the appellant, Gujarat State Civil Supplies Corporation, defendant in the civil suit, the plaintiff had supplied pulses which had impurities.
However, trial Court held that the tests conducted by the Food and Drug Laboratory, Vadodara was contrary to the procedure laid down under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
The HC-NIC Page 1 of 2 Created On Wed Sep 30 01:18:25 IST 2015 trial Court, therefore, came to the conclusion that no reliance can be placed on the findings of such testing.

sentences.text: Being a money decree and considering the findings of the trial Court, we cannot allow the appellant to enjoy unconditional stay.
The appellant, applicant shall, therefore, deposit the entire decreetal amount latest by 15th November, 2015 before the trial Court.
Upon such deposit, it would be open for the respondent, original plaintiff to withdraw the same by offering immovable security to the satisfaction of the Court below.
